summary: Anil Kumar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hyderabad in 2012 and held a post there.

Anil Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (PhD). In 1988 he founded Sandhaan, where he served as Director (attested 1999).

Animesh Prakash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Hong Kong (2016–2017) and was an Assistant Professor at Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2014–2018) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2018).

Animesh Roy focuses on Indology and philosophy. He completed an integrated MA in Sanskrit at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (2017–2022) and became a Research Scholar at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in 2022.
Animisha Tewari specializes in philosophy and Indology. She completed a BA at Miranda House (2017–2020) and an MA at the University of Delhi (2020–2022).

Anirban Dash works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as a Research Assistant (attested 2003–2005) and later as Associate Professor of Sanskrit (attested 2026).
Anita is an Indology scholar who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Lucknow. She became a professor at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith in 2009.

Anjay Dhanawade specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He earned a BA from the University of Mumbai, an MA from Savitribai Phule Pune University, and a PhD from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2010–2016), serving as assistant professor at Lokavikas Samajik Sanstha (2010–2023).
Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami. She served as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Ankita Nanda specializes in Indology. She completed her Ph.D. in 2022 at Panjab University, where she also served as a Senior Research Scholar in 2022.

Ankur Barua works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong, supervised by Dorothy C. Wong, and held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the Australian National University (attested 1983), studying under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Chicago (~1971–1984), and held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (~2000; 2003–2012), where she became professor and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Ann Laura Stoler works in history, archaeology, and other fields. Educated at Barnard College and Columbia University, she taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and the University of Michigan (1989–2004) before becoming founding director at The New School (2004).
Anna Andreeva is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University (attested 2026).

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg University, the University of Würzburg, and the University of Tübingen (MA, 1998). She held posts at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan, and held posts at the Bulletin of Tibetology and Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (2002).

Anna Brown is a scholar of religious studies and other fields who studied Zen under Robert Kennedy. Attested in 2017, she served at Saint Peter's University as political science department chair and social justice program director.
